cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work almost everywhere; cash is rarely needed.
name: Brisbane
tagline: Riverside sunshine, koalas and island day trips
summary: Brisbane is Queensland's easy-going river city, with a man-made beach at South Bank, CityCat ferries and a subtropical climate. Cuddle a koala at Lone Pine, climb the Story Bridge, browse the galleries at GOMA and day-trip to Moreton Island's dunes or the Gold Coast surf.
seasonNote: Autumn to spring (April to September) is warm and dry; summer is hot, humid and stormy.
arrival: Brisbane Airport is 20 minutes from the city on the Airtrain.
gettingAround: Free CityHopper ferries, CityCats and buses with a go card or tap-on bank card.
foodTip: Moreton Bay bugs, Queensland mangoes and riverside brunch.
buyTip: Australian-made fashion in James Street and Indigenous art.

items.name: South Bank Parklands
items.summary: Riverside parkland with a free lagoon beach, gardens and the Wheel of Brisbane.
items.tip: Swim at Streets Beach, then walk the Grand Arbour.

items.name: Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary
items.summary: The world's oldest koala sanctuary, with kangaroos to hand-feed.
items.tip: Arrive by the river cruise from the city.

items.name: GOMA and Queensland Art Gallery
items.summary: Australia's largest modern art gallery, free to enter.

items.name: Story Bridge Adventure Climb
items.summary: Climb the heritage bridge for city and river views.

items.name: Mount Coot-tha Lookout
items.summary: Lookout over the city to Moreton Bay, plus botanic gardens.

items.name: CityCat ferry ride
items.summary: High-speed catamarans along the winding Brisbane River.
items.tip: Ride from UQ to Northshore end to end.

items.name: Moreton Island
items.summary: Sand island with dunes, the Tangalooma wrecks and dolphin feeding.

items.name: Gold Coast beaches
items.summary: Golden surf beaches and high-rises an hour south.
items.tip: Learn to surf at Coolangatta or Burleigh.

items.name: Moreton Bay bugs
items.summary: Sweet slipper lobster from the bay.
items.tip: Order them grilled with garlic butter.

items.name: Eat Street Northshore
items.summary: Night market in shipping containers with food from everywhere.

items.name: Brunch in West End
items.summary: Laid-back cafés with smashed avo and flat whites.

cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work almost everywhere; cash is rarely needed.
name: Cairns
tagline: Gateway to the Great Barrier Reef and the Daintree
summary: Cairns is the tropical base for the Great Barrier Reef and the ancient Daintree Rainforest. Snorkel or dive the outer reef, ride the Skyrail over rainforest to Kuranda, find the beach where rainforest meets reef at Cape Tribulation, and swim in the city's lagoon.
seasonNote: June to October is dry and stinger-free-ish; November to May is the wet season with box jellyfish.
arrival: Cairns Airport is 10 minutes from the Esplanade.
gettingAround: Walk the city; tours pick up from hotels; rent a car for the Daintree.
foodTip: Barramundi, tropical fruit and a sundowner on the Esplanade.
buyTip: Aboriginal art and Kuranda market crafts.

items.name: Outer Great Barrier Reef
items.summary: Full-day boat to the outer reef for snorkelling and diving among coral and turtles.
items.tip: Take a stinger suit and seasickness tablets.

items.name: Skyrail and Kuranda Scenic Railway
items.summary: Cableway over rainforest canopy up, heritage train down.
items.tip: Go up by Skyrail in the morning.

items.name: Daintree and Cape Tribulation
items.summary: The world's oldest rainforest meets the reef on wild beaches.

items.name: Cairns Esplanade Lagoon
items.summary: Free saltwater lagoon pool on the waterfront.
items.tip: Swim here, not in the sea.

items.name: Green Island
items.summary: Coral cay 45 minutes by boat with snorkelling from the beach.

items.name: Crystal Cascades
items.summary: Rainforest swimming holes near town.

items.name: Atherton Tablelands waterfalls
items.summary: Waterfall circuit with Millaa Millaa Falls and crater lakes.

items.name: Barramundi
items.summary: The prized local fish, grilled or battered.
items.tip: Eat on the boardwalk at sunset.

items.name: Cairns Night Markets
items.summary: Food court and souvenir stalls every evening.

items.name: Rusty's Markets
items.summary: Weekend tropical fruit and produce market.

cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work almost everywhere; cash is rarely needed.
name: Perth
tagline: Sunny beaches, quokkas and Swan River sunsets
summary: Perth is one of the sunniest cities on earth, with long white beaches, the vast Kings Park and the riverside port of Fremantle. Ride to Rottnest Island for a quokka selfie, swim at Cottesloe, and drive to the Pinnacles or the Margaret River wine region.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are perfect; summer is hot but great for beaches.
arrival: Perth Airport is 25 minutes from the city by the Airport Line train.
gettingAround: Transperth trains and buses; free CAT buses in the city.
foodTip: Western rock lobster, Margaret River wine and Freo fish and chips.
buyTip: Broome pearls and Margaret River wine.

items.name: Rottnest Island
items.summary: Car-free island of quokkas, turquoise bays and bike trails.
items.expect: Ferry from Fremantle or the city.
items.tip: Rent a bike and snorkel at the Basin.

items.name: Kings Park and Botanic Garden
items.summary: One of the world's largest city parks, with skyline views and a treetop walkway.

items.name: Fremantle
items.summary: Historic port with markets, a convict-built prison and craft breweries.
items.tip: Visit Fremantle Prison and the markets.

items.name: Cottesloe Beach
items.summary: Perth's favourite beach, with sunsets over the Indian Ocean.

items.name: The Pinnacles
items.summary: Thousands of limestone spires in yellow desert.

items.name: Margaret River
items.summary: Wine region with surf beaches and caves.

items.name: Elizabeth Quay
items.summary: Waterfront promenade with the Spanda sculpture and ferries.
items.tip: Walk on to the Bell Tower.

items.name: Fish and chips in Fremantle
items.summary: Fish and chips by the harbour.

items.name: Northbridge
items.summary: Perth's food and nightlife district.

items.name: Western rock lobster
items.summary: Local rock lobster, in season November to June.

cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work almost everywhere; carry a little cash for rural honesty boxes.
name: Rotorua
tagline: Geysers, Māori culture and bubbling mud
summary: Rotorua is New Zealand's geothermal heartland, smelling faintly of sulphur, with spouting geysers, rainbow-coloured hot pools and a living Māori culture. Watch Pōhutu geyser erupt, join a hāngī feast, soak in hot springs and mountain-bike the giant redwoods.
seasonNote: Summer is warm; the steam looks even more dramatic in winter.
arrival: Rotorua Airport is 10 minutes away; Auckland is a 3-hour drive.
gettingAround: A car is best; tours pick up from hotels.

items.name: Te Puia and Pōhutu Geyser
items.summary: Geothermal valley with the southern hemisphere's biggest geyser and a Māori arts institute.
items.tip: Stay for the evening show and hāngī.

items.name: Wai-O-Tapu Thermal Wonderland
items.summary: Champagne Pool and Lady Knox Geyser in vivid colours.

items.name: Māori cultural evening and hāngī
items.summary: Welcome ceremony, haka and a hāngī feast.

items.name: Redwoods Treewalk
items.summary: Suspension bridges among giant redwoods, lit with lanterns at night.

items.name: Polynesian Spa
items.summary: Hot mineral pools by the lake.

items.name: Hobbiton Movie Set
items.summary: The Shire film set with hobbit holes and the Green Dragon Inn.

items.name: Skyline Rotorua gondola and luge
items.summary: Gondola up for lake views and luge rides down.

items.name: Hāngī feast
items.summary: Meat and vegetables slow-cooked in an earth oven.

items.name: Eat Streat
items.summary: Covered street of restaurants with geothermally heated floors.

items.name: Rotorua Night Market
items.summary: Thursday night street market with food trucks and local crafts.
items.tip: Try a hāngī pie or steamed pudding.

cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work almost everywhere; carry a little cash for rural honesty boxes.
name: Wellington
tagline: Windy, creative capital with Te Papa and craft coffee
summary: Wellington is New Zealand's compact capital, wrapped around a harbour, with a red cable car, the superb national museum Te Papa and a famous café and craft beer scene. It is also the home of the film studios behind The Lord of the Rings and the ferry port to the South Island.
seasonNote: Summer is mild; it is windy all year, so bring a jacket.
arrival: Wellington Airport is 15 minutes from the centre by Airport Express bus.
gettingAround: Walk the waterfront; buses and the cable car.
foodTip: Flat whites, craft beer and Wellington on a Plate dishes.
baseArea: Te Aro, Cuba Street or the waterfront

items.name: Te Papa Tongarewa
items.wiki: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa
items.summary: The free national museum, with Māori treasures, a colossal squid and the Gallipoli exhibition.
items.tip: Do not miss Gallipoli: The Scale of Our War.

items.name: Wellington Cable Car
items.summary: Red funicular up to the Botanic Garden and views.
items.tip: Walk back down through the gardens.

items.name: Mount Victoria Lookout
items.summary: Panoramic city lookout with the Hobbit hideaway film spot nearby.

items.name: Wētā Workshop
items.summary: Tour the special-effects workshop behind Lord of the Rings.

items.name: Zealandia Ecosanctuary
items.summary: Predator-free valley full of rare native birds.
items.tip: Take the night tour for kiwi.

items.name: Parliament and the Beehive
items.summary: Free tours of NZ's Parliament.

items.name: Cuba Street
items.summary: Bohemian strip of cafés, bars and street food.

items.name: Harbourside Market
items.summary: Sunday market with produce and street food.

items.name: Craft beer bars
items.summary: Wellington is NZ's craft beer capital.

cashTip: Resorts take cards; carry Fijian dollars for markets, village visits and sevusevu kava gifts.
name: Fiji · Nadi and the islands
summary: Fiji's islands are fringed by soft coral reefs and white beaches, with famously warm hospitality. Base yourself near Nadi or Denarau, then island-hop the Mamanucas and Yasawas, snorkel with manta rays, visit a village for a kava ceremony and soak in the Sabeto mud pools.
seasonNote: May to October is dry and cooler; November to April is hot, wet and cyclone season.
arrival: Nadi International Airport; boats leave from Port Denarau.
gettingAround: Island ferries (Yasawa Flyer), seaplanes and taxis.
foodTip: Kokoda (raw fish in coconut) and lovo feasts.
buyTip: Tapa cloth, wood carvings and Fiji Water souvenirs.
baseArea: Denarau, the Coral Coast or an island resort

items.name: Mamanuca Islands
items.summary: Palm-fringed islands with resorts, snorkelling and Cloud 9's floating bar.
items.tip: Visit Monuriki, the Cast Away island.

items.name: Yasawa Islands
items.summary: Remote volcanic islands with manta ray swims and caves.
items.tip: Swim with mantas May to October.

items.name: Sabeto Mud Pools
items.summary: Paint yourself in mud and soak in hot springs.
items.tip: Combine with the Garden of the Sleeping Giant.

items.name: Garden of the Sleeping Giant
items.summary: Orchid garden at the foot of the mountains.

items.name: Village visit and kava ceremony
items.summary: Join a sevusevu kava ceremony in a traditional village.
items.tip: Bring kava root as a gift.

items.name: Sri Siva Subramaniya Temple
items.summary: The largest Hindu temple in the southern hemisphere.

items.name: Coral Coast and Sigatoka Dunes
items.summary: Sand dunes, reef beaches and river safaris.

items.name: Kokoda
items.summary: Raw fish cured in lime and coconut milk.

items.name: Lovo feast
items.summary: Earth-oven feast of meat, fish and root crops.

items.name: Nadi Market
items.summary: Produce market with kava and curries.

cashTip: Prices are shown in euros; locally you pay in CFP francs (XPF), pegged at about 119 XPF to 1 euro. Resorts take cards; carry some francs for snacks and boats.
name: Bora Bora
tagline: Overwater bungalows on the bluest lagoon
summary: Bora Bora is the dream South Pacific island: a jagged volcanic peak rising from a turquoise lagoon ringed by motu islets. Stay in an overwater bungalow, snorkel with rays and blacktip sharks, take a lagoon tour with a motu picnic and hike or 4x4 up for views.
seasonNote: May to October is dry and breezy; November to April is hot and rainy.
arrival: Fly from Tahiti (Papeete) in 50 minutes; resort boats meet you at the airport motu.
gettingAround: Resort boats and shuttles; bikes and scooters on the main island.
foodTip: Poisson cru and Tahitian vanilla desserts.
buyTip: Tahitian black pearls and monoi oil.
baseArea: A motu resort or Matira Point

items.name: Lagoon tour with rays and sharks
items.summary: Boat tour to snorkel with stingrays, blacktip sharks and coral gardens.
items.tip: Choose a tour with a motu lunch.

items.name: Matira Beach
items.summary: The island's best public beach, with soft sand and shallow water.

items.name: Mount Otemanu 4x4 tour
items.summary: Off-road trip to WWII cannons and lagoon views.

items.name: Coral Gardens
items.summary: Shallow coral reef with tropical fish.

items.name: Vaitape village
items.summary: Main village with pearl shops and a small market.

items.name: Mount Pahia hike
items.summary: Steep guided hike to the summit for epic lagoon views.

items.name: Poisson cru
items.summary: Raw tuna in lime and coconut milk.

items.name: Bloody Mary's
items.summary: Famous sand-floored restaurant with fresh fish.
items.tip: Pick your fish at the counter.

items.name: Roulottes
items.summary: Food trucks serving crêpes, chow mein and poisson cru.
